key_insight: A local open-weight OCR+LLM pipeline can accurately turn faxed referral packets into structured clinical data on a consumer GPU without fabricating facts.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce manual chart review burden and help protect PHI by keeping extraction entirely on-premises for oncology referral workflows.
method: Generated 200 synthetic colorectal cancer referral packets from simulated records and rendered them as fax images with no text layer.
Used OvisOCR2 to transcribe packets and Qwen3.8-27B to extract structured clinical fields.
Scored 20 outcome types against ground truth on 140 validation packets.
evidence_signal: Across 7,879 laboratory values, 99.7% of dates, and 100% of diagnoses were extracted correctly, with weighted accuracy of 0.990 and no fabricated facts among 11,993 extracted facts.
watch_item: Results were based on synthetic referral packets, so real-world fax variability, OCR noise, and site-specific document formats may reduce performance.
paper_title: Extraction of clinical information from faxed medical records using a small local large language model pipeline on consumer hardware
